Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

   - concise summaries with ROUGE-L F1 >= 0.45 on your internal chart notes
   - <10% hallucination threshold on a 300-case spot-check

2) Recommended models to include in the benchmark (based on latency & your budget):

4) Next steps (requested owners & timelines):
   - Alyssa: confirm target 300-case sample and permission to host encrypted sample on Redwood (you can S3 presign or send CSV). Deadline: Feb 17.
   - Helix procurement: if you want Redwood to host an eval dataset in your VPC, share PO/contract constraints.
   - Karthik/Marissa: once we have dataset, we’ll run the automated benchmark (~48 hours) and share a scoring breakdown + failure cases.

Notes on quality regressions you asked about: we will run differential checks versus your current production model (if provided). The rubric flags regressions >5% drop in key metrics and will surface example traces for triage. We can also pin a canary model and roll back if we detect production-impacting regressions during experimentation.

If that all looks good I’ll follow up with the exact CSV schema and a sample row.

Nice — answers inline below and a few clarifications.

A1 (CSV schema): The template expects one row per case. Preferred columns: case_id, clinic_id, encounter_text (raw clinician note), patient_age_bucket, expected_entities (JSON-array string), expected_summary, annotation_quality (manual flag). We can accept pre-parsed tables but please keep the original note as well when possible. I attached a sample row in redwood_eval_template.csv.

A2 (hallucination definition): Good question — for this benchmark we split hallucination into two checks: 
  - entity hallucination: model invents entities not present in the source note (scored per-entity).
  - factual/summary hallucination: model asserts events or outcomes not supported by the note (scored at the summary level). The rubric has explicit examples and a binary flag + severity weight.

Operational notes:
- Scoring: automated scorers run NER F1 and ROUGE-L for summaries. A small manual spot-check (30 cases) will be run for hallucination labels.
- Turnaround: once we have the sanitized CSV and your baseline export we’ll run the automated suite (48–72 hours), then deliver a report with failure buckets and 20 prioritized traces for you to review.

If you can send the sanitized sample by Feb 17 I’ll schedule the run for Feb 18 and share results on Feb 20.

Karthik

- Signed SToU or a short MSA addendum for hosted evals (we can generate a 1-page addendum).

Pricing note: hosting and running the benchmark (3 models, automated scorers, 30-case manual spot-check) is included as part of our evaluation bundle for proof-of-concept customers; any extended retention or Dedicated capacity for longer-term testing will be scoped separately.
